assumptions.unit: days from the demo clock date; minutes; UTC HH:MM daily start times
assumptions.basis: Plausible synthetic handover slots: two clear days to prepare the car, three days of choice and hour-long slots at two daily times. Not retailer calendar data; revisable here.
A half hour of demo time before the synthetic retailer answers a request makes the wait visible on a presenter tick. The call timeout bounds a stalled provider. Revisable demo assumptions.

value.proposalReason: The retailer proposed a different time.

assumptions.unit: difficult-case switch; alternative slot rule; reason text
assumptions.basis: Difficult-case switch for the synthetic provider. Off by default; when on, the provider answers with the next daily slot instead of the requested one and Paula must accept it.

requested.nextStep: Waiting for the retailer to confirm your slot.

change-proposed.nextStep: Accept the new time to confirm your handover.

scheduled.nextStep: The retailer prepares your car for the handover.

ineligible.nextStep: Waiting for your order to be sent to ordering.

pending.nextStep: Waiting for the scheme team to confirm the last update.

blocked.nextStep: The scheme team will review why this was not accepted.

assumptions.unit: owner and next-step label per appointment state
assumptions.basis: Who acts next at each appointment state (HLD review Q19). Owners are Paula (employee), the retailer or the scheme team; labels are concise demo copy, not BMW workflow text.

tooEarly.nextStep: The handover outcome can be recorded once the booked slot starts.

assumptions.unit: seconds of demo time after the booked slot start; owner and next-step label for an early outcome
assumptions.basis: Handover outcome timing (FUCQ-260): a handover can only be completed, or recorded as missed, once its booked slot has started. Zero seconds is the plainest plausible rule; a grace period for a late arrival is set here without code changes.

no-show.nextStep: Your handover was missed. Choose a new slot to rebook.

notReady.nextStep: The retailer finishes the documents and car preparation before the handover.

assumptions.unit: lifecycle exception type key; owner and next-step label per terminal appointment state and per not-ready refusal
assumptions.basis: Terminal handover outcomes (FUCQ-167): completion is allowed only when documents and car readiness are complete, and a missed appointment is reported with the keyed exception type. A completed handover is shown as the final order-progress stage named here (FUCQ-253). Nothing is left for the employee after completion, so its owner is the retailer that recorded the handover, as for a confirmed return (FUCQ-261). Owners and copy are concise demo wording, not BMW workflow text.
